summary: The note is a fiction-book excerpt from the author's collection, in which the narrator explains his practice of writing stories titled after famous science fiction works as commentaries, criticisms, or parodies of the field's cherished ideas. It names several such stories (Anda's Game, I, Robot, True Names, The Man Who Sold the Moon, Jeffty is Five) and traces the publication history of Anda's Game. The main narrative then follows twelve-year-old Anda, who switches to a girl-shaped avatar in an online game after meeting Liza the Organiza, a confident Australian player who addresses the girls at her school assembly.
one_line: A fiction excerpt in which the author describes his sf-parody story series and the Anda's Game narrative about a girl gamer meeting Liza the Organiza.
key_facts: The author decided to write stories with the same titles as famous science fiction works, making each a commentary, criticism, or parody of the field's cherished ideas.
Anda's Game was the first story in this series.
The author was almost finished with a story called True Names that he and Ben Rosenbaum had been tossing back and forth.
The author planned the next stories in the series to be The Man Who Sold the Moon and then maybe Jeffty is Five.
Anda's Game was sold to Salon and later reprinted in Michael Chabon's Best American Short Stories.
The story was podcasted by retired pro Quake player Alice Taylor for the author's podcast.
Anda initially played a boy-elf because her parents had sternly warned her that playing a girl made her an instant perv-magnet.
Anda was 12 years old when she began playing the game as a girl-shaped avatar.
Anda attended Ada Lovelace Comprehensive, where none of the girls would have been caught dead playing a girl character.
Anda called the sexualized girl avatars played by boys 'Bintware'.
Anda met Liza the Organiza, whose female avatar had sensible armor and a large sword.
Liza the Organiza spoke with an Australian accent and addressed the assembled girls at the school as 'chickens'.
Liza was called to the school assembly stage in front of principal Miss Cruickshanks and counsellor Mrs Danzig.
Liza showed the girls a space-themed game on her laptop, with a space-station and a rocketship in the background.
